comparison.definition: Ranking or magnitude across CATEGORIES or against a target — 'how do these things measure up against each other?'. The x-dimension is categorical or a fixed benchmark, not a continuum.
comparison.notFor: A continuous time axis (that is change-over-time), the SHAPE of a single variable's spread (distribution), or parts summing to a whole (composition).

change-over-time.definition: Movement of one or more measures along a TIME continuum — trend, direction, volatility, rate of change. Time is the ordered axis and the reading is the path, not the individual value.
change-over-time.notFor: Unordered categories (comparison), or a snapshot share-of-total with no time dimension (composition).

distribution.definition: The SHAPE of values within one or more variables — frequency, spread, centre, skew, outliers. The reading is the population, not any single member.
distribution.notFor: Naming a winner between categories (comparison) or relating two measures to each other (relationship).

relationship.definition: Correlation or connection BETWEEN two or more quantitative measures — 'does this move with that?'. Both axes carry measures; the point cloud, not the axis order, is the message.
relationship.notFor: One measure over an ordered time axis (change-over-time) or one variable's spread alone (distribution).

composition.definition: Parts of a WHOLE — share, proportion, breakdown that sums to 100%. The reading is the split, and the total is meaningful.
composition.notFor: Comparing independent quantities that do not sum to a whole (comparison), or the spread of a single variable (distribution).

one-number.definition: A single headline figure the reader takes in at a glance — 'what is the number?'. Optionally with its delta and period; never a series.
one-number.notFor: A series or trend (change-over-time), several numbers compared (comparison), or a status word (status-of-one).
one-number.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

status-of-one.definition: The state of ONE thing as a word or colour — 'is it ok?'. Live / paused / failed.
status-of-one.notFor: A count of things in each state (a counting intent), or a magnitude (one-number).
status-of-one.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

details-before-commit.definition: The facts of an action laid out for review before or after it is taken — 'is this what I meant?'. A payment review, a receipt.
details-before-commit.notFor: A running status board, or a KPI figure (one-number).
details-before-commit.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

where-am-i.definition: The reader's position in the hierarchy — 'where am I?'.
where-am-i.notFor: Where the reader can go next (where-can-i-go), or what the current thing is (what-is-this).
where-am-i.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

what-is-this.definition: The name and framing of the thing on screen — 'what is this?'. A page or section header.
what-is-this.notFor: Position in the hierarchy (where-am-i) or available actions (what-can-i-do).
what-is-this.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

what-can-i-do.definition: The actions available to the reader right now — 'what can I do?'.
what-can-i-do.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

where-can-i-go.definition: The destinations the reader can move to — 'where can I go?'. Navigation.
where-can-i-go.notFor: The current position (where-am-i) or actions on this page (what-can-i-do).
where-can-i-go.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

where-does-it-go.definition: How things are placed and spaced on the page — 'where does it go?'. Layout utilities.
where-does-it-go.notFor: The shell that holds the page (what-holds-the-page) or the content itself.
where-does-it-go.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)

what-holds-the-page.definition: The persistent frame around the content — 'what holds the page?'. App shell, top nav.
what-holds-the-page.notFor: Navigation destinations alone (where-can-i-go) or layout spacing (where-does-it-go).
what-holds-the-page.ruled: s253 — chat #253 2026-09-07 Dave: "this sound good to me" on the 9 words page A §14 lists; Claude authors / Dave vetoes (s251-D15)
